title: Analysis of Josephson junctions switching time distributions for the detection of single microwave photons
authors: A. S. Piedjou Komnang, C. Guarcello, C. Barone, C. Gatti, S. Pagano, Vincenzo Pierro, A. Rettaroli, G. Filatrella
abstract: We investigate an optimal scheme for the detection of single microwave photons by a Josephson junction through the analysis of its switching times distribution. The proposed analysis is of support for the decision about the existence of the photon field, which is important in the case of rare events. We assume that the cavity and the transmission line are ideal (each photon absorbed to the cavity gives a current pulse as the output of the transmission line) and the photon source is periodic. The employed methodology consists in comparing the switching probabilities of a Josephson junction exposed to a train of current pulses, simulating a weak photon field, with that of the same device in absence of pulses. In both cases, thermal noise can induce thermal activated switchings. The investigation of the unbalance in the number of switching events in the two cases, gives an estimate of the efficiency of the detection. Furthermore, in the assumption of escapes described by Kramers model, it is possible to provide a relationship between the properties of the photons field, the quantum efficiency of the detection process, and the Josephson junctions switching features at finite temperatures.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to detect single microwave photons using Josephson junctions by analyzing changes in their switching time statistics. It models the junction dynamics using the RCSJ equation and calculates escape rates via the Kramers approximation. The detection performance is quantified using statistical measures like the KC index, providing a pathway to estimate quantum efficiency at finite temperatures.
main_problem: The paper investigates an optimal statistical scheme for detecting the presence of single microwave photons using the switching time distribution of a Josephson junction.
main_result: Detection efficiency can be quantified by analyzing the unbalance in switching events, leading to a relationship between photon field properties, quantum efficiency, and junction switching features at finite temperatures.
method: The analysis compares the switching probabilities of the Josephson junction under two conditions: exposed to a periodic train of current pulses (simulating photons) versus no pulses, utilizing statistical tests like the Kumar-Caroll index.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Josephson Junction modeled by the RCSJ equation, whose dynamics are analyzed via a Langevin equation. The switching process is treated as a noise-induced escape from a metastable washboard potential, governed by the Kramers approximation.
key_observables: Switching time distribution, the Kumar-Caroll (KC) index ($d_{KC}$), and the ratio of switching rates ($r_1/r_0$).
important_parameters: Bias current ($I_b$), noise intensity ($D$), observation time ($P$), and the photon arrival rate ($r_A$).
main_assumptions: Assumes ideal cavity/transmission line, periodic photon source, and utilizes the Kramers model for escape rates; statistical analysis often relies on sample mean approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the electrical model (RCSJ), the pulse train mimicking photon absorption, and the tilted washboard potential showing the trapping and switching dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model (RCSJ, Langevin equation) to deriving the escape rates (Kramers theory). It then develops statistical diagnostics (KC index, dichotomous classification) to quantify detection performance by comparing noise-only vs. signal+noise switching statistics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as it applies non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (Kramers escape rates) to characterize the detection of single quanta (photons) using a superconducting circuit element.
